text:
Matt: Heads up — after last night's router change we're seeing tail latency regressions on mixtral-moe-prod. p99 jumped ~120ms, p999 looks noisy. Change was top_k from 1 -> 2 and a router-softmax tweak. Anyone else seeing this?
Jia: yep, confirmed in staging and prod. KV cache eviction rate spiked ~3x and router CPU is higher. I pulled a quick heatmap — expert load got much less balanced.
perf-bot: [alert] service=mixtral-moe region=us-west shard=shard-5 metric=router_cpu pct95=68 pct99=91 kv_eviction_rate=8.3%
Sam: quick profiler (flamegraph) shows router softmax+topk kernel dominating CPU stack now. Also a lot of time in expert handshake waits (mutex contention). Suspect the top_k change increased routing churn and broke batching alignment.
Jia: also saw more small batches — adaptive batching seems to be splitting awkwardly when multiple experts get chosen for the same request. batching_heuristic=group_by_route flip might have regressed behavior.
Naveen: I ran a short experiment on canary with top_k=3 + router_temp=0.8 and saw router reassignments drop (~30%) but expert saturation increased (per-expert Q depth up). Throughput didn't improve.
Sam: pasted local trace snippet:
```
# perf script extract
router_softmax_kernel  45.2%  (topk+softmax)
kv_cache_lookup        12.1%
expert_handshake_wait  14.8%  (mutex)
batch_coordinator      10.3%
```
Sam: Also noticed kernel selection flipped to cpu_fallback_fused_softmax on some nodes after the rollout (we shipped a kernel selector tweak yesterday). That path is slower for the typical sequence lengths we're seeing.
Jia: can we override kernel selector on a canary to gpu_fused_softmax? That should cut the router CPU. Also we should pin KV entries for hot prefixes to reduce eviction noise.
Matt: proposal for shard-5 canary: revert top_k to 1 on canary, enable kernel_override=gpu_fused_softmax, set sticky_routing_ttl=30s, per_expert_queue_limit=64, and enable kv_pin_for_hot_prefixes. If results look good we can roll to more shards.
Sam: I'll run the canary now. Commands: `deploy --shard shard-5 --overrides "top_k=1,kernel_override=gpu_fused_softmax,sticky_ttl=30,expert_queue=64,kv_pin=true"`
Jia: add dashboards: router_cpu, kv_eviction_rate, expert_q_depth p50/p95/p99 and add regression alerts: router_cpu > 70% AND kv_eviction_rate > 5% for 5m.
perf-bot: Deploy started shard=shard-5 user=Sam at 2026-05-12T03:12:08Z
Sam: 30m into canary: p99 latency improved ~40ms, kv_eviction_rate -> 2.1% (from 8.3%), router_cpu down ~22% on canary nodes. Expert mem usage increased ~7% due to sticky routing & pinned KV entries.
Naveen: 7% mem increase is acceptable for now. But if we see long-term growth we need to TTL-clear pins or LRU degrade. Could also try reducing expert_parallelism (threads/per-expert) to lessen contention.
Matt: good. Plan: keep canary running for 2h, if stable promote. Sam, please run a second run toggling adaptive_batch_split=false to see batch size distribution effect. Jia, add a short eval to ensure quality didn't change with top_k revert.
Sam: will run adaptive_batch_split=false next and post results.
Jia: thanks — also note we should add a small regression test in CI that runs a micro-sim of routing with realistic prefix distribution to catch this earlier.
Matt: agreed. Quick wins: kernel override + sticky routing for now, follow up with batching heuristic fix and CI sim. :thumbsup: 
perf-bot: Canary status update shard=shard-5 uptime=90m p99_delta=-38ms kv_eviction_rate=1.9% expert_mem_delta=+6.8%
Sam: initial verdict — roll forward to 3 additional shards if no new regressions in next 1h. I'll keep posting traces.
Jia: adding dashboard panels and alerts now. If anyone wants the raw trace files ping me and I'll share the perf artifacts.
Matt: thanks team. If we still see hotspots after batching heuristic change, let's schedule a deeper kernel selection audit (compare fused vs split softmax, int8 kernels for short sequences, and linker-level perf flags).
Naveen: +1. Also consider per-customer sticky routing to reduce cold-expert churn for high-QPS tenants.
Sam: noted — filing a follow-up RFC for sticky routing across requests and pinned kv lifecycle.
Matt: perfect — let's keep momentum. :rocket:
